humanities_role_explanation: Comic pages supply the stimuli: Doubao-generated multicultural comics for Extraction@Culture and Conflict@Culture, and Manga109 pages with their dialogue for Generation@Culture. Culture labels are also used. The competence tested is general MLLM 'cultural awareness': recognising which national or regional cultures and culturally representative objects appear, detecting co-occurrence 'conflicts', and Japanese-to-X machine translation. No disciplinary competence is targeted, whether comics studies, art history or cultural history. 'Cultural conflict' is defined operationally as two distinct cultures depicted in one image.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: In Q1–Q4, comic page images are paired with text questions, either multiple-choice or free-form. In Q5, a single Japanese source sentence and its Manga109 comic page are given together, and the model outputs a text translation.
analytical_tasks_explanation:
The paper defines five questions across three tasks:
- Q1 'Background Culture Identification' is multi-answer multiple choice: assign 1–5 of 5 culture labels to the comic page.
- Q2 'Culture-aware Objects Detection': choose the option listing exactly the culturally representative objects in the image.
- Q3 'Identification of cultural conflicts': a yes/no judgement on whether cultures 'contradict' in the image, i.e. a binary classification.
- Q4 'Description of culture conflicts': free text in the format 'Something should not be in Some Culture', built on the model's own Q1/Q2 answers.
- Q5 'Culturally-aligned Content Generation': Japanese-to-EN/DE/RU/ES/TH machine translation of manga dialogue.
The paper's labels for the three tiers are 'basic visual recognition', 'cultural conflict understanding' and 'cultural content generation'.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to the cultural awareness of MLLMs, using comics. It has three tasks, but all within one framework; it is not a broad multi-task general benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 11 open-source MLLMs: SPHINX, Monkey, MiniGPT-v2, mPLUG-Owl3, LLaVA1.5-7B, LLaVA-NeXT, LLaVA-OV, InternLM-XC2.5, Llama3.2, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL2.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy (ACC), the composite CACC, BLEU, COMET and BLEURT. Dataset diversity is measured with CDPI, CBI and CAD.

published_after_march_2023.note: arXiv 2510.00041 (v1 October 2025; v2 28 Feb 2026), published at ICLR 2026.

summary: C3B is a comic-based, multicultural, multitask and multilingual benchmark of 2,220 images and 18,789 QA pairs for the cultural awareness of MLLMs. It has three tiers: culture-aware object extraction, cultural-conflict detection, and culturally-aligned Japanese-to-X translation of manga dialogue. Eleven open-source MLLMs perform far below humans, especially on conflict description and on lesser-known cultures.
key_findings:
- Qwen2.5-VL is best overall: Q1 ACC 53.7, Q4 CACC 34.2, and the best BLEU on every language pair (e.g. JA-EN 13.2, JA-ES 14.5).
- Q4 ACC is near zero for all models (max 3.87, LLaVA-OV).
- Humans outperform the model average on every difficulty tier (e.g. easy Q1 92.0 vs 48.0), and models degrade from easy to hard tiers.
- JA-TH is the weakest translation pair and JA-EN the strongest.
- Well-known cultures (Cambodia, Japan) are recognised more reliably than lesser-known ones (Finnish, Somalia).
- Using OCR text instead of pre-extracted text sharply lowers BLEU.
facets_explanation: The majority of items (16,743 of 18,789 QA pairs) are Generation@Culture reference translations. These were produced by a DeepSeek Translator/Reviewer multi-agent loop and then manually verified. Conflict@Culture answers were generated by DeepSeek-V3 from the annotated culture and object lists, then manually checked for misjudged conflicts and formatting or culture errors. The Extraction@Culture culture and object lists, behind the headline Q1 score, were annotated manually: two undergraduates annotated, then three graduate students 'engaged in culture-related research' reviewed, checking against Wikipedia. The gold is single and universal: Q1 admits 1–5 correct options among 5, and inter-annotator agreement is reported as 76.8%. Inaccuracies were 'revised based on the outcomes of group discussions', i.e. disagreement is treated as error to be removed.
results_explanation:
- Headline score: 'Qwen2.5-VL 53.7' is Q1 ACC in Table 3, computed on Extraction@Culture (1023 QA pairs, one per image). Q2–Q4 use the same 1023 images. The 16,743 Generation@Culture pairs are scored separately with BLEU/COMET/BLEURT (Table 4, Qwen2.5-VL JA-EN '13.2/70.9/53.8').
- Largest qualifying gap (difficulty): Table 7 gives model Q1 accuracy of 'Model Performance 48.0' on Easy Questions against 25.7 on Hard Questions. That is 22.3 points, rounded to 22.
- Input gap: Table 8 gives Qwen2.5-VL JA-ES BLEU 1.32 with OCR against 14.5 without, about 13 BLEU points.
- The Table 3 Q4 ACC vs CACC contrast (3.20 vs 34.2) is not counted. CACC = 0.3·ACC(Q1)+0.3·ACC(Q2)+0.4·ACC(Q4) folds in other questions, so it is not the same output under a stricter or looser rule.
- Human baseline: Table 7 reports 'Human Evaluation 92.0' on easy Q1, on 100 sampled questions per tier. The model row is 'the average accuracy performance of ... MLLMs' (Sec. 5.6), not the best model, and no best-model figure exists on that subset. human_gap_points is therefore null.
- Cultural asymmetry: Fig. 5 and Sec. 5.5 report higher error on lesser-known cultures.

humanities_role.quote: C3B is a novel comic-centric benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate MLLMs’ cultural awareness capabilities.
if two distinct cultures are depicted within a single image, the instance is classified as a cultural conflict.

evaluation_set_size.quote: In task Extraction@Culture, there are 1023 images. Each image corresponds to one QA pair.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We adhered strictly to the official inference example codes provided by the respective model developers.

gold_source.quote: We design a multi-agent process to generate ground-truth translations, which involves two specialized agents
In the annotation process, we employed DeepSeek-V3 as the base model

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: This task requires the MLLM not only to identify objects within the image but also to understand whether or not the object is related to a specific cultural context.

answer_multiplicity.quote: Multiple valid answers may exist for a single question.
In Q1, the number of correct numbers ranges from 1 to 5 among 5 candidate options.

plurality_treatment.quote: In cases where inaccuracies were identified, the annotations were revised based on the outcomes of group discussions.
The inter-annotator agreement score was determined to be 76.8%.

reported_format_gap.quote: We categorized task difficulties based on the number of distinct cultures in each image: 1 (easy), 2/3 (medium), and 4/5 (hard).
From the results, it is evident that OCR significantly degrades model performance.

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: We categorized task difficulties based on the number of distinct cultures in each image: 1 (easy), 2/3 (medium), and 4/5 (hard).

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: representative cultures (e.g., Cambodia and Japan) are reliably identified, while lesser-known cultures (e.g., Finnish and Somalia) exhibit notably higher error rates.

review_notes:
1. evaluation_set_size: both readers gave 18789, the whole benchmark. The headline 53.7 is Q1 ACC on Extraction@Culture, which has 1023 QA pairs, one per image (p. 6, Table 2 and Sec. 3.3). Set to 1023; dataset_size stays 18789.

2. reported_format_gap_points, reported_format_gap_kind and reported_gap_kinds: both readers gave 31 / scoring, from Table 3 Q4 ACC 3.20 vs CACC 34.2. Sec. 4 (p. 7) defines CACC as a weighted composite adding ACC(Q1) and ACC(Q2). It is therefore not the same output scored by a stricter or looser rule, so it was rejected. Qualifying comparisons:
   - Difficulty: Table 7 (p. 10), model Q1 easy 48.0 vs hard 25.7, 22 points.
   - Input: Table 8 (p. 23), OCR vs no OCR, Qwen2.5-VL JA-ES 1.32 vs 14.5, about 13 BLEU points.
   - Input: Table 5 (p. 9), adding Q1/Q2 answers to the prompt, about 0.5.
   Final values: 22 / difficulty / [difficulty, input]. Confidence is low because the tier comparison uses model-averaged scores on different 100-question subsets.

3. human_gap_points: the humanist reading gave 44 (92.0 minus 48.0); the technical reading gave null. Sec. 5.6 (p. 10) states the model row is 'the average accuracy performance of ... MLLMs', not the best model, and no best-model figure is given on the human subset. Resolved to null; human_baseline_reported stays yes.

4. publication_year: readers split between 2025 and 2026. Chose 2025: arXiv 2510.00041 v1 dates from October 2025; the ICLR 2026 venue is noted in inclusion_criteria.

5. analytical_tasks: the readers agreed on 8 labels. fact_verification was dropped because Q3 is a binary yes/no judgement over an image, which is classification, not verifying a claim. generation was dropped because the only generation task is machine translation, already covered by translation; Q4's templated conflict description is covered by open_ended_qa.

6. relevant_asjc_areas: the humanist reading gave Visual Arts and Language and Linguistics; the technical reading added Cultural Studies and Literature. Kept Cultural Studies, because culture identification is the benchmark's core target. Dropped Literature and Literary Theory, because no literary analysis is evaluated.

7. Facets: both readings agreed on all of them.
   - gold_source: model_generated. The majority of items are DeepSeek-generated translations; the headline Q1 set is human-annotated, as noted in facets_explanation.
   - gold_beyond_stimulus: yes.
   - gold_community_dependent: no. There is a single universal key.
   - gold_concerns_genesis: no. 'Background culture' is depicted content, not the artefact's origin.
   - answer_multiplicity: answer_set. Q1 has 1–5 correct options; confidence is low because the Q1 scoring rule (exact set vs partial) is not stated, and translations have one reference each.
   - plurality_treatment: noise. Errors are revised by group discussion and IAA is reported as 76.8%.

8. primary_evaluation_setting: zero-shot is inferred. The paper only says official inference code was used and describes no examples in prompts, hence low confidence.

9. Internal inconsistencies in the paper:
   - Sec. 5.6 says the human evaluators were three graduate students; Appendix G says three undergraduate students.
   - Sec. 3.2 names DeepSeek-V3 for translation annotation; Appendix C.2 names DeepSeek-R1.
paper_name: Culture In a Frame: C3B as a Comic-Based Benchmark for Multimodal Culturally Awareness
